notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0007] Money-moving ops accept idempotency_key first: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it before any state validation: if ledgerly.audit.events() already has an entry with that key, return the original result without reapplying. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit.record() entry.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Annotate public functions with return types: Public functions in ledgerly/invoice.py declare explicit return types (e.g. -> Decimal) alongside parameter annotations; keep the stub's signature annotated when implementing it.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money inputs with round_money before storing: Always pass monetary values through `round_money` from `ledgerly.money` before storing them on models or comparing against `ZERO`; never store raw input on `LineItem.unit_price`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with snake_case codes and context: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, and put the offending value or invoice status in the detail string.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0005] Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
  (learned from task E03 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver (FIN-2026-03): accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing; amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

item.title: Money-moving ops take idempotency_key and check it first
item.content: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. capture in ledgerly/payments.py, refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key: str | None = None`. Check the key against ledgerly.audit.events() before validating state and return the original result if it matches, and include `idempotency_key` in the audit.record(...) call.
